ORIGINAL PAPER



Liouville theorems for nonnegative solutions
to Hardy–Hénon type system on a half space

Wei Dai1,2      · Shaolong Peng1,3

Received: 16 May 2021 / Accepted: 16 November 2021 / Published online: 6 December 2021
© Tusi Mathematical Research Group (TMRG) 2021



Abstract
In this paper, we are concerned with the Hardy–Hénon type system on a half space
ℝn+
                  {       𝛼
                     (−Δ) 2 u(x) = f (x, v), u(x) ≥ 0, x ∈ ℝn+ ,
                          𝛽
                     (−Δ) 2 v(x) = g(x, u),  v(x) ≥ 0, x ∈ ℝn+

with Dirichlet boundary conditions, where n ≥ 1, n > max{𝛼, 𝛽} and 0 < 𝛼, 𝛽 ≤ 2.
We derive Liouville theorems (i.e., the non-existence of nontrivial nonnegative
solutions) provided that f and g satisfy certain subcritical growth conditions (see
Theorem 1.6). The argument used in our proof is the method of scaling spheres
developed in Dai and Qin (Liouville type theorems for fractional and higher order
Hénon–Hardy type equations via the method of scaling spheres, preprint, submit-
ted for publication, p 52, arXiv:​ 1810.​02752). Our results generalize the Liouville
theorems for single Lane–Emden equation in Chen et al. (Adv Math 274: 167–
198, 2015) and Hardy–Hénon type equation in (Dai and Qin arXiv:​ 1810.​02752) to
system and the Liouville theorems for system of Lane–Emden equations ( f = vp,
g = uq ) in Dai et al. LPotential Anal 46:569–588, 2017) to system of equations with
general Hardy–Hénon type nonlinearities f(x, v) and g(x, u).

Keywords Fractional Laplacians · Hardy–Hénon type system · Nonnegative
solutions · Liouville theorems · Method of scaling spheres

Mathematics Subject Classification 35B53 · 35J30 · 35J91

1 Introduction

In this paper, we will investigate the Liouville property of nonnegative solutions to
Hénon–Hardy type system with Dirichlet boundary conditions on a half space ℝn+

The fractional Laplacian is a nonlocal integral-differential operator. It can be used
to model various physical phenomena, such as turbulence and water waves, rela-
tivistic quantum mechanics of stars, molecular dynamics, and anomalous diffusion
and quasi-geostrophic flows (see [14, 17] and the references therein). The fractional
Laplacian also has various applications in probability and finance (see [1, 16] and
the references therein). In particular, it can also be understood as the infinitesimal
generator of a stable Lévy process (see [1]).
   To introduce assumptions on the nonlinearities f(x, v) and g(x, u), we need the
following definitions.

Definition 1.1 We say that the nonlinear term f has subcritical (critical) growth pro-
vided that
Liouville theorems for nonnegative...                                                Page 3 of 21 12

                                              n+𝛼
                                                   ( 2          n−𝛽
                                                                     )
                                            𝜇 n−𝛼 f 𝜇 n−𝛼 x, 𝜇− n−𝛼 v                         (1.5)

is strictly increasing (invariant) with respect to 𝜇 ≥ 1 or 𝜇 ≤ 1 for all
(x, v) ∈ ℝn+ × ℝ+. The corresponding definitions for g(x, u) can be given similarly by
exchanging 𝛼 and 𝛽.

Definition 1.2 A function h(x, u) is called locally Lipschitz on u in ℝn+ × ℝ+ , pro-
vided that for any u0 ∈ ℝ+ and Ω ⊆ ℝn+ bounded, there exists a (relatively) open
neighborhood U(u0 ) ⊂ ℝ+ , such that h is Lipschitz continuous on u in Ω × U(u0 ).

   Throughout this paper, we assume that the nonlinear terms f(x, v) and g(x, u) have
subcritical or critical growth in the sense of Definition 1.1.
   We need the following three assumptions on the nonlinear terms f(x, v) and
g(x, u).
   (𝐀𝟏 ) If f(x, u) has subcritical growth, then it is nondecreasing about u in ℝn+ × ℝ+ ,
namely

              (x, u), (x, v) ∈ ℝn+ × ℝ+ with u ≤ v implies f (x, u) ≤ f (x, v).               (1.6)

If f(x, u) has critical growth, then it is strictly increasing about u in ℝn+ × ℝ+ , namely,

              (x, u), (x, v) ∈ ℝn+ × ℝ+ with u < v implies f (x, u) < f (x, v).               (1.7)

The same assumptions are also made on the nonlinear term g(x, u).
    (𝐀𝟐 ) There exist 𝜎 < 𝛼 and 𝜃 < 𝛽 , such that |x|𝜎 f (x, u) and |x|𝜃 g(x, u) are locally
Lipschitz on u in ℝn+ × ℝ+ .
    (𝐀𝟑 ) There exist a cone C ⊂ Ω with vertex �
                                               at 0 which contains�the positive xn-axis
(if n = 1, C = ℝ+; if n = 2, for instance, C = x ∈ ℝn+ � xn > √   �x�
                                                                       ), constants C > 0,
                                                                                 n
−𝛼 < a < +∞,          −𝛽 < b < +∞,            1 ≤ p ≤ pc (a) ∶= n+𝛼+2a
                                                                  n−𝛽
                                                                                                and
1 ≤ q ≤ qc (b) ∶= n−𝛼 , such that the nonlinear term
                 n+𝛽+2b


                             f (x, v) ≥ C|x|a vp ,          g(x, u) ≥ C|x|b uq                (1.8)
in C × ℝ+ .
   In particular, if we set 𝛼 = 𝛽 and f = g, PDEs’ system (1.1) will degenerate into
one single Hardy–Hénon type equation
                                        𝛼
                                 (−Δ) 2 u(x) = f (x, u),           x ∈ ℝn+ .                  (1.9)

If f (x, u) = |x|a up, equations (1.9) are called Hénon, Lane–Emden, Hardy equations
for a > 0, a = 0, a < 0, respectively. These equations have diverse and important
applications in conformal geometry and Sobolev inequalities. In particular, in the
case a = 0, (1.9) becomes the well-known Lane–Emden equation, which models
many phenomena in mathematical physics and astrophysics.
   Liouville type theorems for Eq. (1.9) (i.e., the non-existence of nontrivial non-
negative solutions) in the whole space ℝn and the half space ℝn+ have been
12 Page 4 of 21                                                                       W. Dai and S. Peng


extensively studied (c.f. [3–5, 9, 12, 13, 19, 20, 22–26, 29, 30, 33, 34, 36–38, 41,
42, 48, 49] and the references therein). These Liouville theorems, in conjunction
with the blowing up and re-scaling arguments, are crucial in establishing a priori
estimates and hence existence of positive solutions to non-variational boundary
value problems for a class of elliptic equations on bounded domains or Riemann-
ian manifolds with boundaries (c.f. [23, 32, 40]). In [16], Cabré and Tan deal
with equations involving a different kind of fractional operator A 1 . The fractional
                                                                                  2
operators As ( s ∈ (0, 1)) are defined using the spectral decomposition of the
Laplacian −Δ, i.e., As u ∶= ∞        a 𝜆s e , where 𝜆k and ek are eigenvalues and the
                              ∑
                                k=1 k k k
corresponding eigenfunctions for the Laplacian operator −Δ in Ω with homogene-
ous Dirichlet boundary data, while ak represents the projection of u on the direc-
tion ek . Servadei and Valdinoci compares the fractional Laplacians (−Δ)s and the
fractional operators As especially from the spectrum point of view and give their
differences in [44]. The first analysis of fractional systems was carried out by
Dipierro and Pinamonti in [21]. For more works on the Liouville type theorems
for system of Hardy-Hénon type equations, see, e.g., [2, 19, 28, 37, 40, 46, 47,
49] and the references therein.
   In this paper, using the method of scaling spheres developed by Dai and Qin
in [23] (see also [4, 24–26]), we prove Liouville type theorems for nonnega-
tive solutions to the Hardy-Hénon type system (1.1) provided that the nonlinear
terms f and g satisfy the subcritical conditions (in the sense of Definition 1.1) and
assumptions (𝐀𝟏 ), (𝐀𝟐 ), and (𝐀𝟑 ).
   First, we need to show that the nonnegative classical solution (u, v) to PDEs’
system (1.1) also satisfies the following equivalent IEs’ system:
                          {
                             u(x) = ∫ℝn G+𝛼 (x, y)f (y, v(y))dy,
                                        +
                             v(x) = ∫ℝn G+𝛽 (x, y)g(y, u(y))dy,                (1.10)
                                        +


where n ≥ 1, n > max{𝛼, 𝛽} 𝛾
                             , 0 < 𝛼, 𝛽 ≤ 2, and the Green function associated with
Dirichlet problem for (−Δ) 2 (𝛾 ∈ (0, 2] ∩ (0, n)) on ℝn+ is given by
                                                    4xn yn       𝛾
                                      Cn,𝛾          |x−y|2     h 2 −1
                    G+𝛾 (x, y) ∶=                                       n   dh.                 (1.11)
                                    |x − y|n−𝛾 ∫0            (1 + h) 2
We have the following equivalence between PDEs’ system (1.1) and IEs’ system
(1.10).

Theorem 1.3 Assume n ≥ 1, n > max{𝛼, 𝛽}, 0 < 𝛼, 𝛽 ≤ 2, f(x, v) and g(x, u) satisfy
the assumption (𝐀𝟑 ). Suppose (u, v) is a pair of nonnegative solution to PDEs’ sys-
tem (1.1), then (u, v) also solves the IEs’ system (1.10), and vice versa.

Remark 1.4 From the proof of Theorem 1.3 (see Sect. 2), one can observe that,
if f(x, v) and g(x, u) satisfy the assumption (𝐀𝟑 ) with general 1 ≤ p < +∞ and
1 ≤ q < +∞, Theorem 1.3 is still valid.
Liouville theorems for nonnegative...                                               Page 5 of 21 12


   Next, by applying the method of scaling spheres developed in [23] (see also, e.g.,
[4, 23–26]), we can establish the following Liouville type result for IEs’ system
(1.10). For more literature on the classification of solutions and Liouville type theo-
rems for various PDE and IE problems via the methods of moving planes or spheres,
please refer to [5, 6, 8, 11, 12, 18, 20, 22, 31, 33–36, 39, 43, 48, 49] and the refer-
ences therein.

Theorem 1.5 Assume n ≥ 1, n > max{𝛼, 𝛽}, 0 < 𝛼, 𝛽 ≤ 2, f(x, v) and g(x, u) satisfy
assumptions (𝐀𝟏 ), (𝐀𝟐 ) and (𝐀𝟑 ). Suppose (u, v) ∈ C(ℝn+ ) × C(ℝn+ ) is a pair of non-
negative solution to IEs’ system (1.10) on ℝn+, if f(x, v) is subcritical and satisfies
(𝐀𝟑 ) with 1 ≤ p < n+𝛼+2a

rem 1.5, we derive immediately the following Liouville theorem for PDEs’ system
(1.1).

Theorem 1.6 Assume n ≥ 1, n > max{𝛼, 𝛽}, 0 < 𝛼, 𝛽 ≤ 2, f(x, v) and g(x, u) satisfy
assumptions (𝐀𝟏 ), (𝐀𝟐 ) and (𝐀𝟑 ). Suppose (u, v) is a pair of nonnegative classical
solution to PDEs’ system (1.1) on ℝn+, if f(x, v) is subcritical and satisfies (𝐀𝟑 ) with
1 ≤ p < n+𝛼+2a

Remark 1.9 Although systems involving arbitrary number of equations can also be
treated in similar way, we mainly focus on the system consisting of two equations in
this paper for the sake of simplicity. To derive the equivalence between the PDEs’
12 Page 6 of 21                                                                   W. Dai and S. Peng

                                                                              𝛼             𝛽
system (1.1) and the IEs’ system (1.10), we require that (−Δ) 2 u and (−Δ) 2 v are
defined point-wisely and continuous (see, e.g., (2.4) and Lemma 2.1). Thus, the pair
of solutions (u, v) are assumed to be classical in Theorems 1.3 and 1.6. To carry out
the method of scaling spheres to derive Liouville theorem for the equivalent IEs’
system (1.10), we need to assume the continuity on the pair of solutions (u, v) (see,
e.g., (3.1), (3.37), (3.38), and Theorem 3.1).

   In the following, we will use C to denote a general positive constant that may
depend on n, 𝛼 , 𝛽 , 𝜎 , 𝜃 , a, b, p, q, C , u and the cone C , and whose value may differ
from line to line.
   The rest of this paper is arranged as follows. In Section 2, we establish the equiv-
alence between PDEs’ system (1.1) and IEs’ system (1.10). In Section 3, we will use
the method of scaling spheres to prove Theorem 1.5, that is, the Liouville theorem
for IEs’ system (1.10).

   The Liouville theorem for harmonic functions on ℝn+ (i.e., Lemma 2.2 with 𝛼 = 2)

3 Proof of Theorem 1.5

In this section, we will prove Theorem 1.5 via contradiction arguments and the method
of scaling spheres. Without loss of generality, we may
                                                     � assume that f(x, v)�is subcritical
and satisfies (𝐀𝟑 ) with 1 ≤ p < n−𝛽 , the cone C = x ∈ ℝn+ � xn > √
                                 n+𝛼+2a                               �x�
                                                                            if n ≥ 2 and
                                                                                                              n
12 Page 10 of 21                                                              W. Dai and S. Peng


C = ℝ+ if n = 1 in assumption (𝐀𝟑 ). We may also assume that the nonlinear terms
f(x, v) and g(x, u) satisfy subcritical or critical conditions in Definition 1.1 for 𝜇 ≥ 1. If
f(x, v) and g(x, u) satisfy subcritical or critical conditions in Definition 1.1 for 𝜇 ≤ 1, we
only need to carry out calculations and estimates outside the upper half ball B𝜆 (0) ∩ ℝn+
during the scaling spheres procedure.
   The method of scaling spheres mainly consists of three steps. First, the IEs’ sys-
tem (1.10) implies that positive solution (u, v) satisfies the same lower bound as funda-
mental solutions as |x| → +∞. Second, by combining this lower bound with the IEs’
system (1.10) and the scaling spheres procedure, we will get a better lower bound for
positive solution than fundamental solutions. Third, based on the second step, a “Boot-
strap” iteration process in conjunction with the IEs’ system (1.10) will provide better
and better lower bound estimates on the asymptotic behavior of positive solution (u, v)
(see Theorem 3.1), which finally lead to a contradiction with the integrability of solu-
tions indicated by the IEs’ system (1.10) unless the solution (u, v) ≡ (0, 0).
   Now, suppose on the contrary that (u, v) is a pair of nonnegative solution to the
equivalent IEs’ system (1.10), but (u, v) is not identically zero, then one can infer from
the IEs’ system (1.10) that (u, v) is actually a pair of positive solution, i.e., u > 0 and
v > 0 in ℝn+. Moreover, there exists a constant C > 0, such that the positive solution
(u, v) satisfies the following lower bound:
                               𝛼                  𝛼
